::: {#exr-miller-deriv-second-gaussian-kernel}
#### Second derivative of the Gaussian kernel

Find the second derivative of

$$f(x) = \exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}$$
:::

::: {#sol-miller-deriv-second-gaussian-kernel}
From @exr-miller-deriv-gaussian-kernel, the first derivative is $f'(x) = -x\exp{-x^2/2}$. Apply the product rule (@thm-product-rule) to $u(x) = -x$ and $v(x) = \exp{-x^2/2}$:

$$\ba
u'(x) &= -1
\\
v'(x) &= -x\exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}
\ea$$

Therefore:

$$\ba
f''(x) &= u'(x)v(x) + u(x)v'(x)
\\
&= (-1)\exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}} + (-x)\sb{-x\exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}}
\\
&= (x^2 - 1)\exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}
\ea$$
:::
